title: How Tulum Party Runs a High-Volume Content Operation Without a Backend Team
summary: Tulum Party manages events, listings, and editorial at scale with Cosmic as their headless CMS. Here's how a lean team ships content fast without backend overhead.
body_text: The problem every lean content team knows You have events to publish, listings to update, and editorial to ship. Your developer is talented and stretched thin. Every content change that requires backend work is a context switch that slows the whole team down. This is the problem Tulum Party set out to solve when they evaluated their content infrastructure. As a platform covering nightlife, events, and culture in one of the world's most active party destinations, they needed a system that could keep up with a fast-moving editorial calendar without turning every update into a developer ticket. The answer was Cosmic. Who is Tulum Party? Tulum Party is the go-to digital platform for events, nightlife, and cultural experiences in Tulum, Mexico. They manage a high volume of content: event listings, venue profiles, editorial pieces, and curated guides, all published at the pace of a destination that never really slows down. Their audience is global, their content is time-sensitive, and their team is lean by design. The requirements When evaluating a CMS, Tulum Party had clear criteria: A modern, API-first backend that their frontend developers could build against without being constrained by legacy architecture Non-technical editors able to publish and update content without developer involvement Fast time to market so new features and content types could ship without long backend cycles Scalability to handle traffic spikes around major events without infrastructure headaches A clean content model flexible enough to support events, listings, editorial, and more from a single platform Why Cosmic Tulum Party chose Cosmic because it checked every box while removing an entire layer of backend complexity from their stack. As Ronnie Bermejo, Software Engineer and DevOps at Tulum Party, put it: "Cosmic is a modern backend in a box, allowing us to concentrate our developer efforts on front-end activities and ship new features faster. It's truly time to market on steroids!" — Ronnie Bermejo, Software Engineer and DevOps That framing, backend in a box, captures exactly what Cosmic is designed to do for lean teams. The content API, object modeling, media management, and user permissions are all handled. Developers stay on the frontend. Editors stay unblocked. Read the full Tulum Party customer story on cosmicjs.com/customers/tulum-party . How they use Cosmic Tulum Party uses Cosmic to power the full content layer of their platform: Event listings and venue profiles are modeled as structured Cosmic Objects, making them easy to query, filter, and display with their TypeScript SDK Editorial content (guides, roundups, cultural pieces) lives in Cosmic alongside structured data, so the whole content operation runs from one place Non-technical team members manage content directly in the Cosmic dashboard without needing developer access or support The REST API and JavaScript SDK give their frontend team clean, predictable data fetching that integrates with their chosen framework The result: developer time stays focused on the product, not on content plumbing. Adding AI to the workflow Tulum Party is not standing still. Their team is actively exploring Cosmic's built-in AI features for content creation and management, and looking at how to automate internal workflows via the Cosmic API. This is the direction the platform is built for. Cosmic's AI content generation features let editors draft, expand, and refine content directly inside the CMS, without switching tools or waiting on a developer to wire up an external AI integration. For a team publishing at the pace of Tulum's event calendar, that kind of in-platform AI assistance is a real multiplier. Automating repetitive content workflows via the API, think bulk publishing, scheduled updates, event expiry, is the logical next step for a team that has already eliminated backend overhead from their day-to-day. The takeaway for content teams Tulum Party's story is a clear example of what the right content infrastructure actually changes: it shifts developer time from maintenance to product, gives editors real autonomy, and creates room for AI-powered workflows when the team is ready to move there. The stack is straightforward. A modern frontend, a flexible API-first CMS, and a team that no longer has to ask a developer to change a listing. That's the whole model. If your team is still routing content changes through a developer queue, that's the problem Cosmic is built to solve. Start for free or book a quick intro call to see how Cosmic fits your stack. title: Doximity's New Report Finds Adoption of Telemedicine Growing, Majority of Patients Plan for Virtual Care Post-Pandemic
body_text: Over 73% of patients plan to have telemedicine visits after the pandemic; nearly 60% of patients prefer mobile devices for telemedicine; telemedicine adoption among physicians is strong across age, gender and location SAN FRANCISCO, Feb. 16, 2022 – Over 73% of patients plan to continue using telemedicine platforms post-pandemic, according to Doximity’s second edition of its State of Telemedicine Report , which was released today. As part of the report, Doximity, Inc. (NYSE: DOCS), the leading digital platform for U.S. medical professionals, analyzed adoption of telemedicine across its physician user base from January 2020 through June 2021 and conducted a study of patients’ experiences with telemedicine during the same time frame. The survey of 2,000 patients regarding their experiences with telemedicine found that 74% of Black, 73% of Latinx, 77% of Asian and 73% of white patients planned to receive some or all of their care through telemedicine after the pandemic. Additionally, the study revealed that patient adoption of telemedicine has increased year-over-year to 67% in 2021. Nearly 60% of patients chose mobile devices for telemedicine visits. Physicians Across All Ages Adopting Telemedicine Another key finding in the report is the strong adoption of telemedicine by physicians of all ages–from their twenties to beyond their seventies. Adoption of telemedicine was similar among men and women physicians and is almost identical when controlled for specialty, age and location. The report found that medical specialties with the highest adoption of telemedicine include specialties such as endocrinology and oncology, which have a high proportion of patients with chronic illness for whom telemedicine can facilitate continuity of care. As part of the study, Doximity also surveyed over 1,000 physician users and found that over 67% felt that access to telemedicine helped build or maintain trust with patients from historically marginalized communities. “Telemedicine makes it easier for doctors to provide care to a wide range of patients, including many patients who most need expanded access to care,” said Peter Alperin, Vice President of Product, Doximity. “The results of our study suggest doctors and patients alike have found it easy and convenient to adopt telemedicine, so much so that they plan to continue using it after the pandemic.” View Doximity’s second edition State of Telemedicine Report . About Doximity Founded in 2010, Doximity is the leading digital platform for U.S. medical professionals. The company’s network members include over 80% of U.S. physicians across all specialties and practice areas. Doximity provides its verified clinical membership with digital tools built for medicine, enabling them to collaborate with colleagues, stay up to date with the latest medical news and research, manage their careers and conduct virtual patient visits. Doximity’s mission is to help doctors be more productive so they can provide better care for their patients. For more information visit Doximity.com. Doximity Media Contact: pr@doximity.com

title: Jay Ingram, CCIM, a commercial broker and developer with Alton Webb Commercial Real Estate in Shelbyville, has joined German American Bank’s Regional Advisory Board
body_text: German American Bank announces Jay Ingram, CCIM, will serve on the company’s Regional Advisory Board serving the Shelby, Spencer, Owen, Gallatin, Oldham, Jefferson, Bullitt and Hardin County markets in Kentucky. Jay joins current Regional Advisory Board Members Michael Hesketh, John Hollenbach, Ray Leathers, Gregory Mills, Brigitte Owens and Purna Veer. German American Bank’s Regional Advisory Boards provide general business counsel to the local corporate management of German American Bank. They are committed to German American Bank’s mission of being a strong financial services company with local decision making and providing competitive banking solutions to Kentucky communities. “Having a strong, engaged advisory board is incredibly important to our work in the Shelbyville community and the surrounding counties,” said Robbie Houchin, Market President at German American Bank. “These individuals offer valuable insight into the local economy and help guide our decision-making so we can better serve our customers and neighbors. Jay’s deep ties to Shelbyville and his expertise in commercial real estate will be a tremendous asset as we continue building strong relationships and supporting the growth of our community.” Ingram is a graduate of Auburn University and earned a Master’s Degree from Southern Illinois University – Edwardsville. Prior to founding a real estate investing company in 2017 and quickly building a portfolio of commercial and residential properties, he spent two years as a missionary in Asia planting churches and then devoted 13 years to teaching English as a Second Language to students from multiple nationalities while training future educators. Ingram and his wife, Amy, a Shelbyville native and a local ENT doctor, ultimately settled in Shelbyville, Kentucky, with their three children, where he joined the Alton Webb Commercial Real Estate team. He specializes in commercial real estate development, as well as, offering investment analysis, leasing support, and disposition services throughout the Commonwealth. Ingram holds a CCIM (Certified Commercial Investment Member) designation. Share Copy Email

title: AI marketing for BiggerPocket shows 44% gains in premium conversions
summary: Words matter, especially when it comes to email marketing. BiggerPockets, the leading real estate investing community, understood this principle and partnered with us to transform their email engagement strategy. By leveraging tailored messaging, automation, and machine learning, we helped BiggerPockets achieve an impressive 32% gain in email engagement. Here’s how we did it
body_text: Words matter, especially when it comes to email marketing. BiggerPockets, the leading real estate investing community, understood this principle and partnered with us to transform their email engagement strategy. By leveraging tailored messaging, automation, and machine learning, we helped BiggerPockets achieve an impressive 44% gain in paid subscriptions. Here’s how we did it: 1. Personalized Messaging for Different Personas Not all investors are the same, and BiggerPockets knows that. To effectively engage their audience, we developed tailored messaging strategies targeting different investor personas. Whether it was seasoned, educated investors or newbies just starting their real estate journey, we crafted specific messages that resonated with each group. By speaking directly to their needs and interests, we were able to build stronger connections and drive higher engagement rates. 2. Automating Error-Prone Manual Campaign Setups Manual campaign setups can be cumbersome and prone to errors, which can dilute the effectiveness of any marketing effort. We introduced automation into BiggerPockets’ email marketing process, streamlining campaign setups and ensuring consistency across all communications. This not only reduced the risk of human error but also freed up valuable time for their marketing team to focus on strategic initiatives. Automation enabled a smoother, more efficient workflow, ultimately contributing to a significant increase in engagement. 3. Using Machine Learning to Resurrect Dormant Users Re-engaging inactive users is often a challenge for marketers, but we saw it as an opportunity. By leveraging machine learning algorithms, we identified patterns and preferences among dormant users, crafting personalized content that reignited their interest in BiggerPockets’ offerings. This targeted approach helped us bring many users back into the fold, boosting overall engagement and expanding the active user base. One of the Best Perks of the Job One of the most rewarding aspects of working with innovative companies like BiggerPockets is the chance to discover exciting new products and learn about niche markets. Just last week, we had an incredible on-site growth strategy session with the BiggerPockets team. Not only did we discuss strategies, but I also learned a thing or two about Tulsa’s booming real estate scene! After our meeting, I headed back to my Airbnb and started browsing through their impressive book collection. I picked a random book off the shelf, and guess what—it turned out to be one of BiggerPockets' own publications! 👀 A huge shoutout to Eric Harper for hosting us! Your team's energy was contagious, and we look forward to more exciting collaborations ahead!

title: Understanding Sustainable Supply Chains and All You Need To Know To Build One
summary: Explore strategies for building sustainable supply chains that reduce environmental impact, improve efficiency, and promote ethical practices in global business operations.
body_text: There’s no doubt that sustainability is a key factor for businesses of all sizes in staying relevant and competitive. A sustainable supply chain concerns more than the physical planet, however. There are social and economic factors that come into play, too. Sustainable practices can help organizations of all stripes lower their carbon footprint, advance their reputation, and invest in their long-term future. What is a sustainable supply chain? A sustainable supply chain is more than a buzzword. It has real-world implications. This infrastructure refers to a group of organizations and processes that lower environmental impact, advance ethical labor practices, and positively help shape it and the country’s economic future. Stakeholders use it to source raw materials, produce goods, and distribute them using the fewest resources. Why is sustainable supply chain management important? Sustainable supply chain management matters on several fronts in the context of operations. Here are a few of the areas where it can make the greatest impact: Reduced Environmental Impact Taking control of the supply chain can help control waste, save energy, and lower carbon emissions. Enhanced Brand Reputation Showing that you’re committed to following practices that help the planet can lure in customers with those same values who wish to align their spending. Risk Mitigation Taking such an approach can help stakeholders get ahead of supply chain disruptions and oversights. Cost Savings Taking a sustainability-forward approach can lead to cost reduction by way of more efficient practices that limit waste. Regulatory Compliance Sustainability can help company leaders limit their legal exposure and related environmental fines. The 3 Pillars of Sustainable Supply Chain A sustainable supply chain is shaped by three key areas: Environmental Sustainability This means companies do their part to minimize the release of harmful gasses into the ozone. They also are good stewards of water, energy and raw materials. They take water reduction seriously and have programs in place to monitor and adjust consumption as needed. Social Sustainability Under a sustainable supply chain, company leaders have invested in fair labor practices and conditions as well as diversity and inclusion efforts. They’re active and engaged in their communities and give back. Economic Sustainability Company leaders invested in sustainable supply chains do their best to build supply chains that can weather the dynamic nature of the market. Fairtrade and support for small businesses are other priorities. The same goes for continuous improvement and investment in technological advancements that can help companies grow in their area. Benefits of a Sustainable Supply Chain Company leaders, suppliers, and consumers stand to gain a lot from building and maintaining a sustainable supply chain. Here are some of the highlights: Risk and Vulnerability Reduction While there’s no certain way to forecast events like environmental and natural disasters or wars, sustainable practices can help to soften the blow of supply chain disruptions. It’s also worth mentioning that following practices related to labor practices and sourcing can help companies better manage their reputations and limit legal damages. Build and Sustain Brand Loyalty and Reputation Sustainable practices can position a company in a positive light and win over customers who wish to vote with their dollars. Consumers today expect more out of companies. Those who rise to the occasion stand to win on the fronts of loyalty and sustainability. Cost Efficiency Introducing waste reduction activities can help companies save on energy costs while keeping transportation costs lower and staying on schedule. Committing to sustainability can help companies gain a footing in the market and work alongside other industry leaders to build a stronger and more resilient supply chain . Sustainable practices can position a company in a positive light and win over customers who wish to vote with their dollars. How To Build a Sustainable Supply Chain: 10 Tactics A sustainable supply chain is the result of intentional efforts. The best way to create one is by doing the following: 1. Identify Sustainability Issues Within the Supply Chain Stakeholders will need to be intentional about how environmental, social, and economic conditions can contribute to certain outcomes. Evaluate your supply chain through the lens of material sourcing, reduced waste, manufacturing processes, transportation, and other delivery channels. This exercise will bring areas to life that require your attention. 2. Adopt a Circular Supply Chain A circular economy helps you get the greatest lifespan out of your products. This can take the form of a few strategies, such as product design, take-back programs, and closed-loop supply chains. 3. Limit Fuel Consumption or Adopt Sustainable Sources of Energy Committing to this can take the form of a few strategies, such as: Optimizing Transportation Routes: Rely on route optimization software to shorten transportation distances and fuel usage. Mode Shifting: Transition to rail or water transport when feasible. Using Energy-Efficient Facilities: Introduce energy-efficient technologies into operations to lower energy bills. Investing in Renewable Energy: Invest in solar and wind power sources to move away from fossil fuels. 4. Eliminate Dead Mileage When vehicles travel empty between loads, this is wasteful. It is also somewhat preventable. To address this phenomenon, consider the following strategies: Load Consolidation: Merge smaller loads into larger ones to help you conserve costs and energy. Backhaul Optimization: Transport goods in both directions to cut down on waste. Real-Time Load Tracking: Monitor real-time statistics to optimize routes and reduce unnecessary travel. 5. Increase the Use of Recycled and Renewable Materials Recycled and renewable materials, like packaging, can help with your sustainability goals. You should do your best to source products from suppliers that have the same philosophy. 6. Improve Supplier Relationship Management It takes a village to build a sustainable supply chain. With that in mind, you’ll want to place a focus and emphasis on priorities like collaborative partnerships, supplier audits, and supplier education. 7. Promote Sustainability Education Help employees understand what it means to think and act in terms of environmental stewardship. Courses related to topics like waste reduction, energy conservation, and ethical sourcing can be helpful in achieving this goal. 8. Establish Sustainability Goals Define success, track progress, and hold your team accountable to your goals. 9. Adopt Ethical Labor Practices Lead by example. Your supply chain should be a model for others. Work with suppliers to ensure safeguards that protect fair wages, safe working conditions, and labor rights. 10. Reduce Waste Waste reduction will look different at each stage of the supply chain. Strive for efforts to reduce packaging materials, match inventory levels with supply and demand, and recycle waste. Companies that invest in sustainable supply chains do their part in creating a more sustainable future. A few of the most popular ones on the market include: Logiwa WMS This warehouse management system (WMS) can help you take control of inventory management, order fulfillment, and shipping operations. Users can benefit from real-time inventory tracking, barcode scanning, and automated workflows. It works well with many of the mainstream e-commerce platforms and shipping carriers, making it helpful for businesses of all sizes. NetSuite NetSuite can help you take your inventory management , order management, and supply chain planning to the next level. It supports functions like finance and accounting, making it convenient for business leaders wanting simplicity. Netstock Netstock makes it easy to handle all of the details related to stock levels, demand forecasting, and purchase order management. You can use it for greater visibility on inventory levels, to lower stockout situations, and to take more control of supply chain intricacies. Precoro Precoro is your one-size-fits-all solution to refining the procurement process, from purchase requests to invoice processing. Users find it helps them bring clarity to procurement operations, reduce costs, and improve compliance. Precoro easily integrates with other software, which is another reason some professionals like to use it. Magaya Supply Chain Magaya Supply Chain supports freight management, customs brokerage, and trade compliance activities. Business people can use it to better understand the nuances of supply chain operations and navigate laws related to customs. SAP SCM SAP SCM’’s appeal is that its scope is far-reaching, from demand planning to transportation management. It may be better suited for large enterprises. FreightPOP Business leaders can look to FreightPOP to keep shipping costs more manageable and improve efficiency. Among its highlights include carrier-rate negotiation, shipment tracking, and customs clearance. Shippo Shippo is ideal for e-commerce businesses because it allows for label printing, shipping rate comparison, and seamless shipping. Oracle Oracle’s extensive offerings are great for supply chain planning, execution, and analytics. Blue Yonder Blue Yonder is a go-to for demand planning, inventory optimization, and transportation management. Manhattan Associates SCM Manhattan Associates SCM can be your secret weapon in warehouse management, transportation management, and taking omnichannel commerce to new heights. Kinaxis RapidResponse Kinaxis RapidResponse’s cloud-based solutions help businesses resolve supply chain disruptions so they can stay competitive. Users find value in its uses for demand planning, supply chain network design, and inventory optimization. title: Transforme gastos com IA em eficiência financeira: empresas estão usando cartão corporativo para pagar ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude e outras plataformas
summary: Empresas estão investindo cada vez mais em ferramentas de Inteligência Artificial. Descubra como transformar esses gastos recorrentes em eficiência financeira utilizando o cartão corporativo do Stark Bank e recebendo 1,5% de cashback.
body_text: A Inteligência Artificial deixou de ser uma iniciativa experimental para se tornar parte da infraestrutura operacional das empresas. Ferramentas como ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, Perplexity, Cursor, GitHub Copilot, Midjourney e plataformas de cloud com recursos de IA passaram a ocupar uma linha cada vez mais relevante nos centros de custo de tecnologia, marketing, produto, operações e atendimento. O que antes representava um investimento pontual em inovação tornou-se uma despesa recorrente e estratégica. Segundo projeções da Gartner, os investimentos globais em Inteligência Artificial generativa devem alcançar US$ 644 bilhões em 2025, um crescimento de 76% em relação ao ano anterior. A consultoria estima ainda que a IA se tornará parte estrutural da operação das empresas, deixando de ser uma iniciativa isolada para se integrar ao cotidiano corporativo. Nesse contexto, surge uma pergunta pouco discutida pelas empresas: se o investimento em IA é inevitável, como transformar esse gasto em mais eficiência financeira? A resposta pode estar justamente na forma como essas despesas são pagas. O crescimento dos gastos corporativos com Inteligência Artificial A corrida pela adoção de Inteligência Artificial está criando uma nova categoria de despesas recorrentes dentro das empresas. Além das assinaturas tradicionais, cresce rapidamente o consumo baseado em uso, especialmente em plataformas de LLMs, APIs e agentes autônomos de IA. Grandes empresas já começaram a implementar políticas específicas para controlar gastos com tokens, limites de consumo e governança financeira das aplicações de IA. Segundo a IDC, o mercado global de Inteligência Artificial movimentará mais de US$ 630 bilhões até 2028, impulsionado principalmente pelos setores de software, serviços financeiros e varejo. Na prática, isso significa que empresas estão aumentando seus gastos mensais com ferramentas como: ChatGPT Team e Enterprise; Google Gemini; Claude; Perplexity; GitHub Copilot; Cursor; OpenAI API; Anthropic API; AWS, Google Cloud e Azure com workloads de IA; plataformas de automação e agentes inteligentes. O desafio é que, embora esses investimentos sejam fundamentais para aumentar produtividade e competitividade, eles continuam sendo registrados apenas como despesas operacionais. title: Constant Tax Law Changes Shouldn't Be a Problem for Tax Pros
summary: Tax laws change frequently, making it difficult for tax professionals and business owners to keep up. Just as you get accustomed to one set of rules, a new set of changes is introduced.
body_text: ‍ How can you stay informed? One of the most straightforward ways to stay on top of these changes is by making regular reading a habit. Financial literature, business periodicals, and reputable publications like the IRS are excellent resources to get updates about proposed and passed tax laws. The more you read, the better prepared you’ll be to handle whatever changes come your way. Networking with other tax professionals through conferences, workshops, or local business groups is another valuable strategy. Sharing knowledge and insights with peers can help you catch important details you might otherwise miss. Continuous education is a must in this field. Taking refresher courses or using online educational tools can help you stay sharp and up to date with the latest changes. The IRS website offers a wealth of information that can be particularly useful. How leveraging technology can help in staying ahead? The tech world is changing and so is the tax industry. Tax professionals are now switching to AI-powered tools to stay informed and gain a competitive edge. Advanced tax tools are now becoming a part of their regular practice. These tools provide regular updates, alerts, and scenario analysis to help them stay compliant and make informed decisions. If you want to make your tax service more efficient and valuable, TaxGPT offers 24/7 access to the latest tax information. It allows you to find accurate answers to complex tax questions quickly with the updated credible tax sources. Looking at the response below, you can see how TaxGPT keeps you ahead of the game with constant changes in tax laws, like the IRS's new tax inflation adjustments for the 2024 tax year. It breaks down the latest updates—whether it's changes to standard deductions, new marginal tax rates, or adjustments for the Earned Income Tax Credit—so you don't have to. Instead of spending hours trying to make sense of new regulations, TaxGPT delivers the latest information directly to you, clearly and accurately. With tools like this, you get real-time updates and straightforward answers to complex questions, making it easier to stay compliant and informed.
